Hi Sam — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery: 

- Primary concern: ensure customer PII is protected (masking/encryption at rest and in transit).
- Data retention: FinTrust needs 90/180/365-day retention tiers configurable per dataset.
- Logging/audit: detailed admin & support access logs retained for 12 months; ability to export audit trails.
- Access controls: RBAC with least-privilege defaults; ability to define custom roles; formal break-glass for emergency support with multi-party approval and post-event audit.
- Data residency: production deployments must be in us-east-1 (no cross-region replication without approval).

Next steps I proposed on the call: 
1) I send a short write-up with how Redwood handles RBAC, support access, and break-glass procedures (attachments).

Hi Sam — following up with the technical details we discussed and answers to the specific asks: 

1) RBAC & least privilege
- Redwood provides role-based access with a set of built-in roles (admin, developer, support, auditor).
- Customers can create custom roles scoped to projects/datasets with fine-grained permissions (read/write/manage/retention-policy).
- Default provisioning uses least-privilege templates; we expose an API and Console UI for role assignment and change history.

2) Support access & break-glass
- Redwood support does NOT have standing access to customer data.
- Emergency (break-glass) access is available via an auditable workflow: 
  * Request initiated in Console or via ticket and requires two approvers (customer-designated approver + Redwood on-call manager).
  * Access granted is time-limited (configurable, defaults to 1 hour) and scoped to the minimal dataset needed.
  * All break-glass events generate: approver IDs, justification text, start/end timestamps, and a generated audit package (logs + snapshot) for post-event review.
  * Notifications: immediate email to customer security mailbox + webhook option.

3) Logging & retention controls
- Audit logs capture all admin/support actions, API calls, and break-glass events. Logs are immutable and stored in our encrypted logging cluster.
- Retention policies: configurable by dataset or environment (90/180/365 days or custom).
- Legal hold: we support retention hold flags that prevent deletion until the hold is released; holds are visible in the Console and via API.
- Exports: audit logs and access reports can be exported as .csv or supplied as a DLP package for compliance review.

4) Data residency & encryption
- Production deployments can be pinned to region (us-east-1 in your case). No cross-region replication unless explicitly enabled by account owners.
- Data is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS1.2+). Customer-managed KMS is supported for Dedicated/Private deployments.

I've attached a short SOC2 summary and an access_control_matrix that maps Redwood roles to FinTrust requirements. The SOC2 summary is a one-page run-down — full report available under NDA.

Let me know if you want a quick call to walk through the matrix. We can also add a sample break-glass audit package to the export for your team to review.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
